The user wants me to propose a CI optimization based on evidence. Let me analyze the situation.

Original workflow:
```yaml
name: Lint
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [ '24' ]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
#          cache: npm

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint:ci
```

The workflow runs lint only (no tests). It has a single job "test" with a matrix of one node version. It uses checkout v4 and setup-node v4. The cache line is commented out.

Evidence available:
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: measured experiment on a fork, adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job. Baseline median elapsed 41s, optimized 30s, 26.8% savings. This is a measured CI workflow on fork evidence. The artifact before/after shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to the job.
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: dependency cache pattern, but it's literature/analyst example, not measured on this repo. The workflow has cache commented out. But the pattern says "Mutable or untrusted cached content" contraindication, and "An equivalent cache already exists". The cache line is commented out, so no equivalent cache exists. But this is not measured evidence for this repo; it's literature report.

The instruction says: "Propose any evidence-supported CI optimization that fits this workflow; there is no fixed optimization-type allowlist. Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes. Use retrieved evidence and repository files to check prerequisites."

The strongest evidence is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT which is a measured CI workflow on fork (evidence_scope: measured_ci_workflow_on_fork). It shows adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to a job reduced elapsed time from 41s to 30s (26.8% savings) with same success count (3/3).

The workflow here is a lint workflow that runs npm ci and lint. A custom timeout of 5 minutes seems reasonable for a lint job. The evidence directly supports adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to the job.

Prerequisites check:
- The pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". The repository context shows CI history with 5 runs, all success, durations around 35 seconds (18:10:31 to 18:11:06 = 35s, 18:08:16 to 18:08:43 = 27s, etc.). So representative successful-duration history exists (runs complete in ~27-39 seconds).
- Contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". The runs complete in under 40 seconds, so a 5-minute timeout is generous and won't cut off valid runs.

The evidence ID: document_id "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508" with pattern_id "P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT". Also the pattern catalogue entry "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT".

The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one." So I should cite evidence_ids. Which IDs are supported? The evidence chunks have document_id values. Let me use the experiment document_id: "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508". Also possibly the pattern catalogue document_id "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT". The instruction says "Use only supported evidence IDs". I'll include the experiment document_id and maybe the pattern id. Let me include both to be safe but they must be supported. The evidence list includes document_id "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508" (chunks 0 and 1) and pattern catalogue entries. I'll cite "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508" and "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT".

This repo's lint job has representative successful history (~27-39s across 5 runs), all well under 5 minutes, so a 5-minute bound prevents runaway consumption without cutting valid runs. Coverage unchanged (still runs lint:ci on push main and PRs). No new network, secrets, or privileged actions.
